rationale: This is a mechanical product of two archived signals and is near-duplicative of "Historical Inventory Accrual Exposure" (same TS_RANK(invt/at,3) gate on essentially the same accrual construct), with the only change being a 3-year bounded accrual share, so it is a cosmetic recombination rather than a new mechanism.

Dropping capx from the denominator of the archived "Intangible Capitalization Allocation" is a cosmetic variant that leaves the signal a near-monotone transform of Δintan/dpc and does nothing to diagnose why that parent's strong FMB slope failed to translate into portfolio alpha.

The one-sided truncation is a substantively motivated response to a real, documented FMB-versus-alpha sign conflict in the parent signal (disposals/restructurings versus noncash additions), the expression correctly implements max(x,0) via x+|x|, and the expected negative sign matches the construction—though the mass of ties at zero should be checked for unstable portfolio composition.

The persistence plus one-sided accrual gate is a defensible, non-cosmetic reworking of the archived issuance-accrual interaction, but it changes two things at once and the strictly nonnegative signal will pile most firms at zero, so the short leg's identity needs verification.

The expression matches the hypothesis and the one-sided gate is a genuine structural change from the archived rank-product version, but abandoning IND_RANK reintroduces raw-scale and outlier sensitivity in noisy emp-based growth, and the parent already delivered reliable alpha so the diagnosed "nonmonotonicity" is asserted rather than evidenced.

Positive-part net investment (capx−dp)/lagged assets is essentially the long-published capital-investment/net-investment anomaly with a trivial truncation, involves no cross-theme interaction despite the "conditional" label, and adds little beyond the archived absolute-mismatch variant.
